gre-readiness-check-verbal-134.prompt: The documentarian's footage was ______ about working conditions, yet her narration was openly ______ toward the mill owners she named on camera.

options.a: tendentious .. evenhanded
options.b: incurious .. nonpartisan
options.c: perfunctory .. equivocal
options.d: exacting .. partisan

gre-readiness-check-verbal-134.explanation: The contrast is accuracy in the images versus advocacy in the voice-over. Exacting matches scrupulous visual evidence; partisan matches taking a side against named owners without pretending to be neutral.

distractorExplanations.a: Tendentious footage would already be slanted, and evenhanded narration would cancel the open stance toward the owners.
distractorExplanations.b: Incurious contradicts careful filming of conditions; nonpartisan contradicts openly taking a side.
distractorExplanations.c: Perfunctory filming is careless, not evidence-heavy, and equivocal narration refuses the clear stance.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-135.prompt: A lab compared solvers of multi-step logic puzzles. One group had a two-minute cap; another could take as long as needed. Unlimited-time solvers were more accurate and later reported less regret. A third condition that required listing two rejected options before choosing raised satisfaction further, though sessions ran longer. Which inference is best supported?

options.a: Extra time and considering alternatives improved quality, at a cost in speed
options.b: A two-minute cap ruins accuracy on every kind of problem people face
options.c: Stress, not the clock, is the only driver of puzzle accuracy
options.d: Listing rejected options wipes out all later regret about the choice

gre-readiness-check-verbal-135.explanation: Unlimited time improved accuracy and reduced regret; listing rejected options raised satisfaction while lengthening the session. Together those results support a quality–speed trade-off, not a claim that time pressure always fails or that one tactic erases regret entirely.

distractorExplanations.b: The study used logic puzzles with a two-minute cap; it does not license 'every kind of problem.'
distractorExplanations.c: Stress is not measured; the manipulated variable is time, plus listing alternatives.
distractorExplanations.d: Listing alternatives raised satisfaction; it is not said to eliminate all regret.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-136.prompt: The paleographer ______ every charter against the original ink, then ______ the founding myths those charters had long been used to prop up.

options.a: skimmed .. consecrated
options.b: collated .. punctured
options.c: rushed .. venerated
options.d: verified .. deferred to

gre-readiness-check-verbal-136.explanation: Collated captures line-by-line checking of documents; punctured captures knocking holes in the myths the documents had supported. The stem pairs archival care with willingness to overturn received stories.

distractorExplanations.a: Skimming is the opposite of checking originals; consecrating myths would preserve them, not challenge them.
distractorExplanations.c: Rushing contradicts careful ink comparison; venerating myths contradicts dismantling them.
distractorExplanations.d: Verified fits the first blank, but deferred to would keep the founding myths intact.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-137.prompt: A mill let line workers vote on weekly production targets. Those workers reported stronger loyalty to the plant and also more evening strain about missed quotas. Plants that only added a suggestion box saw smaller loyalty gains and no extra strain. Which conclusion is most directly supported?

options.a: Any hierarchy on a shop floor is bound to fail modern plants
options.b: Flexible hours, not voice, drive loyalty in this mill study
options.c: Real say over targets raised both commitment and strain
options.d: Suggestion boxes beat voting for keeping turnover low

gre-readiness-check-verbal-137.explanation: Workers who voted on targets showed both greater loyalty and more strain about quotas. The suggestion-box plants did not show that dual pattern, so the supported claim is that genuine input raised commitment and stress together.

distractorExplanations.a: The passage never calls hierarchy inherently ineffective; it reports one voice intervention.
distractorExplanations.b: Scheduling is not discussed; the contrast is voting versus a suggestion box.
distractorExplanations.d: Suggestion boxes produced smaller loyalty gains, not a win on turnover.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-138.prompt: In a paper on rush-hour gridlock, an engineer calls stop-and-go waves 'emergent.' In that usage she most nearly means that the waves

options.a: appear only among the newest drivers on a given corridor
options.b: are fading because GPS apps have already ended congestion
options.c: can be filmed solely at solstice festivals on already closed roads
options.d: arise from many local braking choices, not a single planned jam

gre-readiness-check-verbal-138.explanation: In this traffic-engineering sense, emergent patterns are not designed by a central planner. They appear when many drivers slow for the car ahead, producing a wave that no one scheduled.

distractorExplanations.a: Age of drivers is not what emergence names; the term is about unplanned collective pattern.
distractorExplanations.b: Emergence is origin from interaction, not a claim that congestion is disappearing.
distractorExplanations.c: Seasonal filming windows confuse emergence with a calendar of special events.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-139.prompt: The quartet's first movement was ______ in layout—key changes arrived without warning—yet an inner pulse kept the movement from collapsing into mere ______.

options.a: labyrinthine .. noise
options.b: foreseeable .. novelty
options.c: textbook .. sweetness
options.d: childlike .. density

gre-readiness-check-verbal-139.explanation: Labyrinthine fits surprise key changes in a still-coherent form. Noise is what the inner pulse prevents: disorder without musical sense. The pairing is maze-like structure that still holds together.

distractorExplanations.b: Foreseeable layout contradicts unheralded key changes.
distractorExplanations.c: Textbook layout would not surprise listeners with sudden harmonic turns.
distractorExplanations.d: Childlike layout understates the complexity; density is not what coherence is said to prevent.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-140.prompt: Students who closed the textbook and wrote what they remembered from a chapter scored higher two weeks later than classmates who reread the same pages. Mixing those self-tests across two rooms transferred better to a new exam format. Cramming in one sitting lagged spaced self-tests on a delayed quiz. Which inference is strongest?

options.a: Pairing pictures with audio is the cheapest way to lock in a chapter
options.b: Retrieving from memory beat rereading for later retention
options.c: A gym session matters more than sleep for any later quiz
options.d: Spacing helps only if the rooms used for study always differ

gre-readiness-check-verbal-140.explanation: The head-to-head contrast is closed-book recall versus rereading, and recall won after two weeks. Other methods appear, but the supported inference is that retrieval outperformed passive review.

distractorExplanations.a: Dual encoding is not tested here; the contrast is retrieval versus rereading.
distractorExplanations.c: Exercise and sleep are not in this design, so neither can be ranked.
distractorExplanations.d: Two rooms helped transfer; the passage does not make mixed rooms a requirement for spacing to work.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-141.prompt: The field botanist's plots were ______ in layout—every quadrat mapped—yet she stayed ______ when an unexpected hybrid appeared and wrecked her first species list.

options.a: flashy .. hidebound
options.b: sloppy .. stubborn
options.c: orderly .. adaptive
options.d: painstaking .. partisan

gre-readiness-check-verbal-141.explanation: Mapped quadrats are orderly; willingness to revise the species list after a surprise hybrid is adaptive. Good field practice pairs a tight grid with readiness to change the hypothesis.

distractorExplanations.a: Flashy does not describe mapped quadrats; hidebound would refuse the hybrid, not accommodate it.
distractorExplanations.b: Sloppy contradicts mapped plots; stubborn contradicts revising the list.
distractorExplanations.d: Painstaking could fit mapping, but partisan does not name openness to an unexpected find.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-142.prompt: Kindergarteners hearing two languages at home sorted shapes by a new rule faster than monolingual classmates and recovered more quickly after a naming slip. Children learning a second script also did better on a block-copying task. Heritage-language evenings tracked stronger family identity talk, not weaker school scores. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.a: Home-language evenings left no trace in the children's lives
options.b: Tonal languages should be dropped because reading in school always lags
options.c: One-language classrooms beat two-language homes on every test
options.d: Early dual-language exposure tracked advantages outside speech alone

gre-readiness-check-verbal-142.explanation: Rule-shifting, recovery from naming errors, and block-copying are not speech tests. The passage ties those gains to bilingual or biscript exposure, so the fair conclusion is cognitive carryover beyond language skill.

distractorExplanations.a: Heritage evenings tracked stronger identity talk, so they were not without effect.
distractorExplanations.b: Tonal languages are not discussed; the passage does not urge dropping them.
distractorExplanations.c: Monolingual peers were slower on the rule-shift task, not uniformly superior.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-143.prompt: A furniture critic praises a bench for 'material honesty.' In that usage she most nearly means that the maker

options.a: lets oak grain and peg joints stay visible rather than veneered
options.b: chooses only imported hardwoods priced for luxury showroom floors
options.c: carves the bench into a miniature copy of a famous palace hall
options.d: prints a plaque listing every designer who influenced the form

gre-readiness-check-verbal-143.explanation: Material honesty in craft criticism is showing what the stuff is—grain, joinery, finish—instead of disguising wood as stone or hiding joints under veneer. Cost, pictorial copying, and influence lists are other virtues.

distractorExplanations.b: Price and import status are not what honesty of material names.
distractorExplanations.c: Likeness to a palace is pictorial representation, not candor about wood and joints.
distractorExplanations.d: Crediting influences is intellectual citation, not how the bench is built.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-144.prompt: Reviewers granted that the treatise's proofs were ______, but they called the last chapter ______, as if all that machinery had been built to announce a slogan.

options.a: plain .. ornate
options.b: knotty .. thin
options.c: strict .. misty
options.d: leaky .. rich

gre-readiness-check-verbal-144.explanation: Yet-logic: complex proofs (knotty) ending in a slogan-like last chapter (thin). Critics wanted nuance from heavy machinery, not a simplified punch line.

distractorExplanations.a: Plain proofs plus ornate endings invert the complaint that complexity yielded a slogan.
distractorExplanations.c: Misty would mean unclear endings; the charge is oversimplification, not fog.
distractorExplanations.d: Leaky proofs would be the problem, not praised machinery; rich endings would not be slogans.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-145.prompt: Cities that added dedicated bus lanes cut peak congestion more than cities that only widened beltways. Where bike-share docks sat next to those lanes, per-capita exhaust fell. A downtown cordon toll cleared midday smog further. Shop streets rebuilt for walking reported higher receipts despite higher first-year paving bills. Which inference is strongest?

options.a: Widening beltways is the cheapest lasting fix for every metro jam
options.b: Walkable streets always bankrupt the cities that try them
options.c: Transit-first packages showed gains beyond thinner traffic
options.d: Density alone sets commute length in every metro studied

gre-readiness-check-verbal-145.explanation: Bus lanes reduced congestion, bike-share tracked lower exhaust, the toll tracked clearer air, and walking streets tracked sales. That is a bundle of effects, not traffic relief alone.

distractorExplanations.a: Beltway widening lost the congestion comparison to bus lanes.
distractorExplanations.b: Higher paving costs sat beside higher receipts, not proven bankruptcy.
distractorExplanations.d: The passage never isolates density as the sole commute driver.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-146.prompt: The courtyard designer insisted each wall answer its own sun and wind, a ______ habit her rivals called ______ because the four sides no longer read as one composition.

options.a: doctrinaire .. signature
options.b: novel .. blended
options.c: thrifty .. colossal
options.d: site-led .. piecemeal

gre-readiness-check-verbal-146.explanation: Responding wall-by-wall to sun and wind is site-led. Rivals who miss a single composition call that piecemeal. The pairing is her principle versus their charge of incoherence.

distractorExplanations.a: Doctrinaire universal rules are what she refused; signature would not be their complaint of incoherence.
distractorExplanations.b: Blended sides would be the opposite of the charge that the courtyard fails as one composition.
distractorExplanations.c: Thrifty and colossal do not map onto microclimate response versus visual unity.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-147.prompt: No-take oyster reefs held more species than fished flats. Beds downstream of sewage outfalls bleached more often. Crews that reset shell after storms saw faster rebound, at a standing labor cost. Deeper beds swung less with heat spikes. Which conclusion is most directly supported?

options.a: Less harvest pressure helped, and restocking sped recovery after storms
options.b: Only no-take rules can keep any oyster bed alive in this warm water
options.c: Depth alone decides whether a bed survives a heat week
options.d: Resetting shell after storms costs too much to be worth trying

gre-readiness-check-verbal-147.explanation: No-take beds were richer in species, and restocked shell recovered faster after storms. Those two results support reduced harvest plus active reset, without claiming either lever is the only one that works.

distractorExplanations.b: 'Only' overreaches; pollution, depth, and restocking also appear.
distractorExplanations.c: Depth reduced heat swing; it is not named as the sole survival factor.
distractorExplanations.d: Labor cost is noted; the passage still reports faster rebound, not a verdict of waste.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-148.prompt: A critic of compact lyrics praises their 'semantic density.' She most nearly means that the lines

options.a: hide the sense on purpose so only insiders can decode them
options.b: pack several claims or allusions into a short run of words
options.c: obey a strict inherited meter and end-rhyme scheme throughout
options.d: prefer snapshot images and refuse any abstract noun at all

gre-readiness-check-verbal-148.explanation: Semantic density is meaning per word: stacked allusion and implication in a small space. Obscurity, meter, and image-versus-abstraction are neighboring but different charges.

distractorExplanations.a: Difficulty can result from density, but the term names concentration of sense, not a lockout policy.
distractorExplanations.c: Inherited form is metrics, not how much meaning each line carries.
distractorExplanations.d: Concrete imagery is a style choice; density can be abstract or concrete.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-149.prompt: The tax model's equations were ______ enough to impress theorists, yet ______ enough that a city budget office could run them before a vote.

options.a: bookish .. ornamental
options.b: tangled .. dumbed-down
options.c: refined .. usable
options.d: airy .. tactile

gre-readiness-check-verbal-149.explanation: The stem wants intellectual polish plus implementability. Refined matches equations that impress theorists; usable matches a budget office running them before a vote.

distractorExplanations.a: Ornamental models would not be run before a vote; bookish misses the elegance-plus-use pairing.
distractorExplanations.b: Dumbed-down contradicts impressing theorists while remaining workable.
distractorExplanations.d: Airy versus tactile is a texture contrast, not elegance versus policy use.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-150.prompt: A focus study found that a daily silent sit improved vigilance on a long monitoring task. Silencing phones during the same task raised completion rates. Timed pauses every ninety minutes kept afternoon scores from sliding. North-facing windows reduced reported fatigue. None of the tactics was tested as the unique best. Which inference is strongest?

options.a: Silent sitting is the single best available fix for every vigilance lapse
options.b: Room light barely matters next to any habit change people try
options.c: Phones are the only real obstacle to finishing office work
options.d: Several independent tactics each improved some attention measure

gre-readiness-check-verbal-150.explanation: Meditation, phone silence, pauses, and daylight each moved a different metric, and the design did not crown a winner. The supported inference is multiple helpful tactics, not a single cause.

distractorExplanations.a: Silent sitting helped vigilance; it is not ranked as the unique best.
distractorExplanations.b: Windows reduced fatigue, so environment is not dismissed as trivial.
distractorExplanations.c: Phones mattered for completion; other tactics also moved scores.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-151.prompt: Unlike chronicles that either gild an empire or write it off as cruelty alone, this account is ______, crediting canals and recording the corvée that built them.

options.a: even-tempered
options.b: doctrinaire
options.c: cursory
options.d: self-canceling

gre-readiness-check-verbal-151.explanation: The writer refuses both gold-leaf praise and total dismissal, holding canals and forced labor in one frame. Even-tempered names that refusal of extremes.

distractorExplanations.b: Doctrinaire history would pick one camp, not hold both canals and corvée.
distractorExplanations.c: Cursory work would skip the double accounting the stem describes.
distractorExplanations.d: Recording two facts is not a contradiction; it is a balanced ledger.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-152.prompt: Shoppers given an extra minute in a mock aisle bought fewer impulse add-ons. Those who jotted two pluses and minuses before tapping 'buy' later said they were happier with the cart. A brief chat with a partner cut regret but slowed checkout. Instinct-first shoppers finished fastest. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.a: Speed always improves the cart when the mock aisle is complicated
options.b: Slowing down traded time for fewer impulses and more satisfaction
options.c: Past grocery trips remove any need to list pluses and minuses
options.d: A partner chat is the strongest single way to cut every error

gre-readiness-check-verbal-152.explanation: Extra time cut impulse add-ons; listing pluses and minuses raised later satisfaction; talking slowed checkout. That pattern is a deliberation–speed trade-off, not a claim that speed always wins.

distractorExplanations.a: Fast instinct shoppers finished sooner; the passage does not say their carts were better.
distractorExplanations.c: Prior experience is not shown to erase the benefit of listing reasons.
distractorExplanations.d: Partner chat cut regret; it is not ranked as the strongest error-cutter.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-153.prompt: Late in her career the novelist grew more ______ with form—chapters arrived as letters, then as court minutes—while keeping the ______ plots that first won her a wide audience.

options.a: cautious .. startling
options.b: routine .. thorny
options.c: daring .. readable
options.d: brittle .. elastic

gre-readiness-check-verbal-153.explanation: Letters and court minutes are formal experiments (daring) held inside plots still easy to follow (readable). The stem is innovation of vehicle, not abandonment of audience.

distractorExplanations.a: Cautious form contradicts the unconventional chapter vehicles.
distractorExplanations.b: Routine form contradicts letters-then-minutes; thorny plots would not obviously keep a wide audience.
distractorExplanations.d: Brittle and elastic do not name experiment versus crowd-pleasing story.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-154.prompt: In a talk on Alpine landscapes, a restorer says the far peaks show 'atmospheric perspective.' She most nearly means that those peaks are painted

options.a: with saints in the clouds to signal a religious program
options.b: so faces in the foreground carry extra emotional charge
options.c: outdoors at noon to copy the sun's exact color temperature
options.d: paler and softer-edged than the rocks nearest the viewer

gre-readiness-check-verbal-154.explanation: Atmospheric (aerial) perspective mimics haze: distant forms lose contrast, blue out, and lose edge. It is a depth cue, not a theme, a facial expression, or a plein-air schedule.

distractorExplanations.a: Sacred staffage is iconography, not the haze-and-distance trick.
distractorExplanations.b: Expressive faces are psychology of portraiture, not recession in space.
distractorExplanations.c: Painting outdoors concerns light source, not the specific fade of distant forms.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-155.prompt: Woodlots given a cool prescribed burn grew native understory faster than lots left untouched. Light browsing kept more plant species than total deer exclusion, which later wilted in a dry year. Edge lots near suburbs recovered slower yet kept rarer orchids under extra patrols. Which inference is strongest?

options.a: Modest disturbance here aided recovery more than total hands-off
options.b: Suburb edges always doom a woodlot even with extra orchid patrols
options.c: Barring every deer and flame produces the most resilient stand
options.d: A nearby creek is the only factor that ever restores a canopy

gre-readiness-check-verbal-155.explanation: Cool fire sped native understory; moderate browsing beat total exclusion on diversity and drought. Those results support modest disturbance over a total hands-off or no-deer policy.

distractorExplanations.b: Edge lots were slower but kept rare orchids; that is mixed, not doomed.
distractorExplanations.c: Total exclusion later wilted in drought, so it is not the resilience winner.
distractorExplanations.d: Water is not isolated as the single restoration cause in this passage.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-156.prompt: Her lab notebooks were ______—each reagent timed to the second—yet the discussion section was ______, leaping from those rows to a sweeping claim about all protein folding.

options.a: tidy .. overly hesitant
options.b: exacting .. audacious
options.c: messy .. timid
options.d: minute .. wary

gre-readiness-check-verbal-156.explanation: Yet marks a split: timed reagents (exacting) versus a sweeping fold-of-all-proteins claim (audacious). Colleagues who call the leap speculative are naming that second blank.

distractorExplanations.a: Hesitant discussion would not be a sweeping claim about all folding.
distractorExplanations.c: Messy notebooks contradict second-by-second timing.
distractorExplanations.d: Wary discussion would pull back, not leap to a global claim.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-157.prompt: Pickers with labeled digital bins closed orders faster than pickers whose desktops were a heap of files. Timed two-hour pauses held accuracy after lunch. Same-day notes on a missed scan improved the next shift, with a brief spike in tension. Short morning huddles cut crossed wires. Which conclusion is most directly supported?

options.a: Open warehouse floors should close because extra talk always kills picking
options.b: Same-day notes fail because any tension spoils later accuracy
options.c: Clear bins and other routines tracked better speed, focus, or coordination
options.d: One software suite is the only driver of on-time warehouse work

gre-readiness-check-verbal-157.explanation: Labeled bins sped orders, pauses held afternoon accuracy, huddles cut crossed wires. The through-line is structured practice, not a single tool or a ban on talking.

distractorExplanations.a: Talk is not shown to ruin picking; huddles helped coordination.
distractorExplanations.b: Tension rose briefly; next-shift accuracy still improved after notes.
distractorExplanations.d: Software is not isolated as the unique productivity cause.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-158.prompt: The gallery hang was ______: white walls, sparse lamps, no wall texts. Detractors called that choice ______, as if the works had been lifted out of the decades that made them.

options.a: busy .. urbane
options.b: baroque .. too naive
options.c: novel .. antique
options.d: spare .. flattening

gre-readiness-check-verbal-158.explanation: White walls and no texts are spare. Critics who miss historical framing call that flattening: the hang subtracts context until the objects look context-free.

distractorExplanations.a: Busy walls contradict sparse lamps and missing texts.
distractorExplanations.b: Baroque display is ornament-heavy, not this stripped hang.
distractorExplanations.c: Antique would not be the charge that context has been stripped from contemporary viewing.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-159.prompt: A program note calls the middle of a fugue 'contrapuntal.' That most nearly means the passage

options.a: lets several melodies proceed on their own while interlocking
options.b: asks the pianist for ever trickier dotted-rhythm stunts on repeats
options.c: jumps through odd chord changes meant to shock the hall
options.d: marks sudden loud-soft swings on almost every measure

gre-readiness-check-verbal-159.explanation: Counterpoint is independent lines that still fit together. Rhythm stunts, shock harmony, and dynamics are other kinds of difficulty.

distractorExplanations.b: Dotted-rhythm difficulty is a rhythmic problem, not multiple independent lines.
distractorExplanations.c: Odd chords are harmonic surprise, not the definition of counterpoint.
distractorExplanations.d: Loud-soft swings are dynamics, unrelated to how lines weave.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-160.prompt: Villages that kept evening story hours retained more place-names than villages that stored lore only in a binder. Councils that could change chairs without a feud adapted faster to a new highway. Households that took phones but kept harvest rites reported tighter neighbor ties, after early pushback. Which inference is strongest?

options.a: Any change to a rite is sure to dissolve a village's identity
options.b: Keeping core rites while taking some tools tracked sturdier cohesion
options.c: Binders always lose to spoken hours for every kind of memory
options.d: Murals, not councils or phones, are what truly hold a village together

gre-readiness-check-verbal-160.explanation: Phones plus kept harvest rites tracked tighter ties; flexible councils adapted; story hours kept names. The pattern is selective mix, not a ban on change or a single art form.

distractorExplanations.a: Selective adoption improved cohesion after pushback; change is not shown as identity death.
distractorExplanations.c: Spoken hours kept more names here; that is not a law about every memory type.
distractorExplanations.d: Art traditions are not the measured driver in this passage.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-161.prompt: The chapel was ______ in finish—bare plaster, uncarved benches—yet visitors spoke of an unexpected ______ that made them sit longer than the guidebook suggested.

options.a: stripped .. chill
options.b: gilded .. plainness
options.c: severe .. welcome
options.d: fussy .. barrenness

gre-readiness-check-verbal-161.explanation: Bare plaster is severe. Sitting longer than the guidebook suggests is welcome, not chill. The 'yet' is austerity that still feels hospitable.

distractorExplanations.a: Chill would not explain lingering past the guidebook time.
distractorExplanations.b: Gilded finish contradicts uncarved benches and bare plaster.
distractorExplanations.d: Fussy finish contradicts the spare interior; barrenness would not invite sitting.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-162.prompt: Children who began a second language before seven were likelier to be judged native-like in accent than those who started after twelve. Daily half-hour talk sped vocabulary. Keeping the home language raised later talk-about-language scores, with a short-lived slowdown in both tongues. Which conclusion is most directly supported?

options.a: Songs beat every other classroom method for a second language
options.b: Daily talk matters more than any correction during conversation
options.c: Keeping the home language always speeds the new language overall from day one
options.d: Age of first exposure tracked accent more than the other measures did

gre-readiness-check-verbal-162.explanation: The sharpest stated contrast is before-seven versus after-twelve accent. Other tactics help vocabulary or metalinguistic skill, but the passage's strongest supported claim is the age–accent link.

distractorExplanations.a: Music is not compared as a superior method in this passage.
distractorExplanations.b: Daily talk and correction are not ranked against each other here.
distractorExplanations.c: Home-language maintenance raised awareness but also a temporary slowdown, so not 'always speeds.'

gre-readiness-check-verbal-163.prompt: A critic says a chapter renders 'fragmented consciousness.' She most nearly means the prose

options.a: follows jumps of thought instead of a tidy chronological plot
options.b: drops periods so that every sentence is left unfinished on the page
options.c: proves the novelist was writing from a diagnosed mental illness
options.d: chooses rare words mainly to keep casual readers from following

gre-readiness-check-verbal-163.explanation: Fragmented consciousness is a modernist way of showing mind: association, interruption, non-linear time. Missing punctuation, biography, and vocabulary snobbery are other complaints.

distractorExplanations.b: Unfinished sentences are a graphic trick, not necessarily a model of mind.
distractorExplanations.c: The term names a technique, not a medical claim about the author.
distractorExplanations.d: Obscure diction is a different device from representing broken attention.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-164.prompt: The envoy's method looked ______—old enemies signed a ceasefire—yet opponents said it was too ______, trading doctrine for a date on a calendar.

options.a: futile .. stiff
options.b: fruitful .. expedient
options.c: divisive .. too utopian
options.d: grand .. cautious

gre-readiness-check-verbal-164.explanation: A signed ceasefire is fruitful. Critics who say doctrine was traded for a date are calling the method expedient: it worked by compromising principle.

distractorExplanations.a: Futile contradicts the signed ceasefire.
distractorExplanations.c: Utopian would cling to doctrine, not be charged with abandoning it.
distractorExplanations.d: Cautious does not capture the charge of sacrificing principle for a date.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-165.prompt: Kelp stands inside a no-take zone recovered from a heat week faster than fished stands. Mixed-species stands held up better in warm water. Fish-rich stands cycled nutrients more cleanly. Moderate swell thickened blades but also snapped more holdfasts in storms. Which inference is strongest?

options.a: Species mix outranks fish biomass for every kelp stability test
options.b: Swell is an unmixed blessing for blades despite storm breakage
options.c: The no-take zone showed the largest named recovery advantage
options.d: Mangrove-like filtering would make harvest limits unnecessary

gre-readiness-check-verbal-165.explanation: The passage's sharpest recovery contrast is no-take versus fished stands after heat. Other factors help, but the strongest single named recovery edge is the protected zone.

distractorExplanations.a: Mix and fish both help; the passage does not rank them for every test.
distractorExplanations.b: Swell thickened blades and increased storm breakage, so it is mixed.
distractorExplanations.d: Filtering is not shown, and it is not said to replace harvest limits.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-166.prompt: The chronicle was ______ in scene—readers almost heard the yard's iron—yet the argument stayed ______, refusing the velvet kings that filler histories prefer.

options.a: theatrical .. badly slanted
options.b: fussy .. personal
options.c: thin .. exhaustive
options.d: vivid .. dispassionate

gre-readiness-check-verbal-166.explanation: Heard iron is vivid scene-making. Refusing velvet-king filler is dispassionate analysis. The pairing is sensory richness without romantic glaze.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-167.prompt: Learners who spread reviews across days kept more of a word list at six months than learners who massed the same minutes in one night. gre-readiness-check-verbal-168.prompt: An essay on a plaza installation praises its 'spatial dialogue.' The critic most nearly means that the pieces

gre-readiness-check-verbal-169.prompt: The kitchen's plates were ______ in look—beans, bread, a tin cup—yet ______ in method, using gels and smokes that made those staples taste unlike the farm table they recalled.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-170.prompt: Ports that shifted containers onto rail for the inland leg cut highway pileups more than ports that only added truck lanes. gre-readiness-check-verbal-171.prompt: Readers said the essays were ______ on the surface and ______ underneath: a high-school class could finish them, a seminar could still argue for an hour.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-172.prompt: High schools that replaced some lectures with multi-week builds saw higher class talk. Flex bells improved attendance. gre-readiness-check-verbal-173.prompt: A housing note calls last year's bidding 'irrational exuberance.' The writer most nearly means that buyers were

gre-readiness-check-verbal-174.prompt: The city's drains and stepped wells were ______ enough that engineers still sketch them, yet the same culture was ______ about foreign tools, copying almost none from ports a week's sail away.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-175.prompt: Ridge gauges on the wet side of a range recorded more yearly rain than same-height gauges on the dry side. Forested soils held more moisture. gre-readiness-check-verbal-176.prompt: Asked whether the merger talks were failing, the referee gave a ______ reply, naming the stalled clauses instead of hiding behind 'no comment.'
